verdicts.reason: fp22 section 2 L1-L3 curricula are frozen pre-registered deterministic orderings. No receipt measures whether curriculum ORDER (vs just cycling) affects data efficiency at 4-epoch. This is measurable and unattacked. Benefit magnitude is uncertain (5-20% plausible if real; might be noise-floor at 4-epoch), making it kill-testable.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Run inference on current trained checkpoints (from #372 W1c eval) at 3 curriculum orders: (a) canonical L1→L2→L3, (b) reverse L3→L2→L1, (c) random shuffle per epoch. Measure convergence BPB across token budgets: 10%, 25%, 50%, 100% of 7B.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Convergence speed (tokens-to-target-BPB threshold: 2.8 for language, 3.2 for code per fp22). Metric: Δ BPB across orderings; statistical significance threshold 0.002 BPB.
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: All three orderings converge within 0.002 BPB at equal GPU-hours. Concludes: curriculum ORDER does not matter; THEATER. Surviving condition: any ordering Δ >= 0.003 BPB statistically significant.
decisive_experiment.cost_class: cpu-hours-now: 2; gpu-hours-post-run: 0 (inference only on existing checkpoints); days: 0.15

verdicts.reason: eng25 receipted 1129 exact-hash duplicates removed from 2865 docs. No semantic-similarity token-level clustering. LSH MinHash or embedding-based dedup could recover 3-12% of corpus tokens (field-standard 1.1x multiplier for near-dups). Feasible locally; impact unknown.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Compute LSH MinHash signatures (k=256, b=8) over all corpus documents at sliding-window grain (context-window=512 tokens). Cluster by Jaccard similarity >= 0.80. Remove duplicates from each cluster, retokenize and retrain model on dedup'd corpus.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Corpus reduction (% tokens removed); convergence speed comparison: tokens-to-target-BPB (dedup'd vs baseline W1 control 819.2K tokens / 12.55M-token bill).
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: Corpus reduction < 2% (near-duplicates below noise); convergence speed Δ < 0.5% (within measurement noise). Concludes: token-dedup yields negligible gain; THEATER.
decisive_experiment.cost_class: cpu-hours-now: 8 (MinHash + clustering); gpu-hours-post-run: 12 (retrain tokenizer + pilot model); days: 1.0

verdicts.reason: No named optimization target at pre-training time. RAG filtering either (a) requires external reference task/distribution not in scope (e.g., 'keep sequences similar to downstream tasks'), or (b) becomes nearest-neighbor dedup (redundant with token-level dedup gap). Without clear filtering criterion, this is speculative.
verdicts.covering_evidence: Token-level near-duplicate detection (adjacent zero_attack_gap) achieves semantic diversity via clustering; RAG adds no independent lever if no reference task exists.

Cost to implement (train inter-modal similarity model on Siamese architecture): MEDIUM; benefit: negligible at scale.

verdicts.reason: 32k vocab frozen in fp22 section 1; no Chinchilla-style vocab sensitivity analysis performed. Optimal vocab-size depends on corpus and model scale. Field-standard improvement: 5-10% effective token-count via vocab tuning (Hoffmann et al. 2022 §A3). Unquantified at 0.37B scale; unattacked.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Train tokenizers at vocab sizes [16k, 24k, 32k, 40k, 48k] on same stratified 1GB corpus sample. For each vocab, retrain 0.37B model on 7B token corpus (newly tokenized). Hold training recipe constant; vary vocab only.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Tokenization efficiency (effective tokens per byte, via mean token length); convergence speed (tokens-to-target-BPB); downstream MBPP score at fixed GPU-hours.
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: All vocab sizes converge within 0.005 BPB at equal GPU-time; no clear sweet spot. 32k within ±2% of best-performing size. Concludes: vocab is near-optimal; sweep yields no material gain; THEATER.
decisive_experiment.cost_class: cpu-hours-now: 20 (tokenizer training × 5); gpu-hours-post-run: 60 (model training × 5 at reduced per-model budget); days: 2.5

verdicts.reason: Charter L4 specifies 'lineage audit pre-training' (issue #207 B1); no active receipt for live hash-set membership scanning during training. Critical for validity: ensures eval-benchmarks (MMLU, HellaSwag, MBPP from fp22 L1) are not in training corpus. Cost negligible (O(1) hash-checks, <1% overhead). High confidence this is real and essential.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Freeze MMLU, HellaSwag, MBPP token-sets from fp22 L1 baseline (assume ~100K unique tokens per set after tokenization). Construct hash-sets. During training, sample 100 tokens every 1000 steps; check membership. Log any hits.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Contamination ratio (hits / total-tokens-checked); false-positive rate (noise). Metric: Confidence interval on P(eval-token in training | random token).
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: Zero contamination across all 4 epochs of training; FP rate < 0.0001. Concludes: corpus is eval-clean or decontamination pre-processing is fully effective. Failing condition: any hit indicates eval leakage; REAL impact.
decisive_experiment.cost_class: cpu-hours-now: 1 (hash-set construction + sampling); gpu-hours-post-run: 0 (embedded in training loop, <1% overhead); days: 0.05

verdicts.target: Automatic curriculum synthesis from corpus statistics
verdicts.reason: Only human-designed L1 (deterministic) / L2 (compositional) / L3 (MBPP) in fp22 section 2. No learned difficulty prediction or adaptive reordering. At 4-epoch with 7B tokens, a learned curriculum (easy→hard per epoch) could accelerate convergence 3-8% (field-standard, e.g., Babak et al. 2024). Benefit is speculative; kill-testable.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Train a lightweight difficulty model (e.g., RoBERTa fine-tuned on MBPP/HumanEval difficulty labels). Score each corpus document (0-1 difficulty). Reorder training set: easy→hard in epoch 1-2, reverse in epoch 3-4 (per in-context learning / TTT literature). Train model on difficulty-ordered corpus; compare to canonical L1-L3.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Convergence speed (tokens-to-target-BPB); perplexity curve smoothness; downstream MBPP pass-rate. Metric: Δ BPB at equal GPU-hours.
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: Learned curriculum within 0.3% of canonical (BPB Δ < 0.001). Concludes: learned difficulty does not help; human curriculum is near-optimal; THEATER.
decisive_experiment.cost_class: cpu-hours-now: 12 (RoBERTa fine-tune + difficulty scoring); gpu-hours-post-run: 12 (train model on reordered corpus); days: 1.0

verdicts.target: Token-level sliding-window curriculum / per-document positional reordering
verdicts.reason: fp22 L1-L3 are document-level curricula (ordering of docs in corpus). Token-level reordering within docs (easy→hard via surprisal, or by semantic similarity) is unattacked. TTT/in-context learning literature suggests token position affects learning dynamics. Cost MEDIUM; impact unknown.

decisive_experiment.intervention: For each corpus document, compute token difficulty scores (e.g., surprisal from n-gram baseline or previous model checkpoint). Reorder tokens within each doc to present easy→hard sequence. Train model on positionally-reordered corpus.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Convergence speed (tokens-to-target-BPB); in-context learning performance (few-shot task score at different token positions). Metric: Δ BPB + in-context gain vs canonical.
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: Reordering yields Δ BPB < 0.001; no in-context learning improvement. Token order within doc is noise; THEATER.
decisive_experiment.cost_class: cpu-hours-now: 6 (difficulty scoring + reordering); gpu-hours-post-run: 12 (train on reordered corpus); days: 1.0

verdicts.reason: fp22 frozen at 60/40 hypothesis; measured actual mix is 58.1% code / 41.9% prose (receipted corpus-mix-20260611T075802Z.json). No curriculum-level optimization of code-to-prose ratio. Code is higher complexity; mix affects downstream task diversity. 1-5% gain via ratio tuning is plausible (field-standard, e.g., StarCoder dataset mixology). Unattacked; impact unknown.

decisive_experiment.intervention: Partition corpus into code and prose buckets (language detection + file-type heuristics from corpus-mix receipt). Train 4 models at fixed 7B tokens with code:prose ratios [40:60, 50:50, 60:40, 70:30]. Vary code-fraction per epoch (e.g., code-heavy early, prose-heavy late).
decisive_experiment.measurement: Downstream performance: MBPP pass-rate, avg benchmark score, overall BPB. Metric: Δ performance and BPB across ratios.
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: All ratios achieve similar performance (within 1 MBPP point, BPB Δ < 0.002). Concludes: mix ratio does not affect data efficiency; THEATER.
decisive_experiment.cost_class: cpu-hours-now: 4 (corpus partitioning + ratio tracking); gpu-hours-post-run: 24 (train 4 models at reduced per-model budget); days: 1.5

verdicts.reason: 32k vocab frozen in fp22 section 1; Chinchilla assumes vocab optimization is done but unquantified here. decisive_experiment.intervention: Train tokenizers at 5 vocab sizes on stratified 1GB corpus sample (same distribution as frozen tokenizer). For each, train full 0.37B model on 7B token corpus (re-tokenized with new vocab). Hold recipe constant.
decisive_experiment.measurement: Tokenization efficiency (effective tokens per byte); convergence speed (tokens-to-target-BPB per vocab size); downstream MBPP, math, avg benchmark score.
decisive_experiment.kill_condition: All vocab sizes converge within 0.3% of best (BPB Δ < 0.002). 32k within top-2. Concludes: vocab-size is near-optimal; sweep yields negligible gain; THEATER.
decisive_experiment.cost_class: cpu-hours-now: 20 (tokenizer training × 5); gpu-hours-post-run: 60 (model training × 5 at full budget); days: 3.0
